comments.text:
Growing up by the sea in a village setting in Fiji, until I was a young adult, I believe is just as complex and demanding an experience as growing up, elsewhere in the world. The major differences, this excellent documentary, had to focus on, are the bio-physical and socio-cultural environments, we grow up in. Growing up in the 60s and 70s, the term Climate Change or its nascent existence was not acknowledged in the media. It was acknowledged by a few physical scientists who had  noted an incremental build up of CO2 in the atmosphere since the beginning of the Industrial Revolution.Their warnings of the multifareous catastrophic impact of Climate Change, if the global build up of greenhouse gases was not reduced or reversed, unfortunately, generally fell on deaf ears. While today, the global community is, accutely aware of the need to reduce or reverse the build up of greenhouse gases, and have instituted some remedial measures, they are mainly promises which have yet to see the light of day.The reluctance of the larger, developed countries mainly responsible for Climate Change, to implement effective  remedial measures in their own countries, is apparent in international conferences on the issue. Meanwhile, vulnerable communities like the Vunidogoloa villagers, whose contribution to the build up of greenhouse gases is negligible, are compelled to relocate to higher ground. What of those Pacifìc communities living on the smaller,flat,
atoll islands with no higher ground to relocate to ?
